upsertSlices.label: Adjacency-matrix access · enumerate then color
upsertSlices.task: Enumerate every possible edge then compute a proper coloring
assumptions: Known vertex set; one unit-cost Pair(u,v) query returns adjacency in a fixed undirected simple graph.
Query every unordered pair u<v once; build a stored graph and compute its maximum degree during the scan.
All actual edges are retained before the randomized static coloring stage; that stage makes no additional matrix-oracle queries.
Explicit output includes a color for every actual edge; absent pairs are not output.
For Δ=0 output is empty; for Δ=1 assign color 1 to each edge in O(m) additional time. The expression log max{2,Δ} extends the displayed time to these trivial cases.

yAxis.label: Pair queries · symbolic asymptotic order
yAxis.note: Ordered asymptotic reference tiers only; the point is Θ(n²), annotated with exact n(n−1)/2. This is not a numeric interpolation or a second result.

parameters.coordinateConvention: Curated figure uses symbolic asymptotic reference tiers, with the exact n(n−1)/2 count attached to the baseline. The single point is at palette Δ+1 and quadratic query order. Computation and output have separate labels.
parameters.density: No dependence on m in the scan query count.

results.bound: Exactly n(n−1)/2 pair queries; after scanning: O(m log max{2,Δ}) w.h.p. computation
results.guarantee: Proper q=Δ+1 edge coloring; randomized computation completes w.h.p.; the pair count is deterministic.
results.sourceLocation: Corollary C.1(1), with proof in §C.1; deterministic matrix enumeration is an atlas derivation.
results.notes: The exact matrix-query count is the cost of this full-scan construction, not a matrix-oracle theorem of the cited paper. The same scan runs on sparse and dense graphs. Theorem 1.1 states O(m log n); the sharper degree-sensitive time comes from Corollary C.1(1). The total time includes enumeration. No query lower bound or oracle optimality is claimed. For Δ=0 output is empty; for Δ=1 assign color 1 to each edge in O(m) additional time. The expression log max{2,Δ} extends the displayed time to these trivial cases.
